belief: I'm not the person I used to be, so I'm less of a person.
origins: After a stroke, concussion, or other brain injury, abilities, personality, and speed can change. Family may say, “You’re not the same,” and the loss of who we were can feel like a loss of value.
teaches: God’s image in us is not tied to speed, memory, or skill: “God created man in His own image” (Genesis 1:27). “Even the very hairs of your head are all numbered” (Luke 12:7). “Though our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.” “Your hands have made me and fashioned me” (Psalm 119:73). God knows you completely and loves you as you are now. Your worth was never your performance. You are still you, and still His.
self_statements: I am a shadow of myself.
I have lost who I was.
errors: Believing I am either who I was or nothing.
Predicting that I will never be myself.
Feeling changed and concluding I am less.
Calling myself less of a person.
questions: What has changed, and what has stayed the same?
What do my loved ones still love about me?
What parts of my character remain, such as kindness, humor, and faith?
What does Scripture say about the source of my worth?
What new strengths or insights have developed?
How can I grieve what has changed and still honor who I am?
truth: My worth rests in God’s image and His love, not in my abilities. I may be changed, but I am not less. I can grieve losses and still live with purpose.
hw_truths: I am made in God’s image.
God knows every hair on my head.
log: Each week, note one thing that is still true of you.
actions: Hear what they treasure about you.
prayer: Lord, I have changed and I mourn who I was. Remind me that my worth is in You, and help me live fully as the person You love now. Amen.
